:::{#def-lower-upper-limits}
#### Lower limit of a sum or integral

In a [sum](algebra.qmd#def-summation) $\sum_{i=m}^{n} a_i$,
the **lower limit** $m$ is the first value of the index $i$.
In an [integral](calculus.qmd#def-riemann-integral) $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$,
the **lower limit** $a$ is the left end of the interval of integration.
In both, the lower limit is written below the symbol.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-upper-limit}
#### Upper limit of a sum or integral

In a [sum](algebra.qmd#def-summation) $\sum_{i=m}^{n} a_i$,
the **upper limit** $n$ is the last value of the index $i$.
In an [integral](calculus.qmd#def-riemann-integral) $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$,
the **upper limit** $b$ is the right end of the interval of integration.
In both, the upper limit is written above the symbol.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-limits-of-integration}
#### Limits of integration

In an [integral](calculus.qmd#def-riemann-integral) $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$,
the lower limit (@def-lower-upper-limits) $a$ and the upper limit (@def-upper-limit) $b$
together are the **limits of integration**.

:::
